title: Sleep vs Timer Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Two timelines on a shared 0-3000 ms axis compare a robot that blinks an LED with sleep() against one that uses a ticks_ms() timer. Students drop an obstacle and measure how long each version takes to detect it and how far the robot travels in that time.

educational.topic: Blocking sleep() delays versus non-blocking ticks_ms() timers
learningObjectives: Compare the obstacle-detection delay of a sleep() loop and a ticks_ms() timer loop.
Explain why a robot that sleeps cannot read its sensor during the sleep.
Relate the worst-case detection delay to the sleep interval and to the sensor check period.
Convert a detection delay into distance traveled at a given robot speed.
prerequisites: sleep(), ticks_ms(), and ticks_diff() from the time module
Speed as distance per unit of time
standards: CSTA 3A-AP-15: Justify the selection of specific control structures when tradeoffs involve implementation, readability, and program performance

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Side-by-side comparison with measurement: predict, drop an obstacle, measure the delay, and vary one setting at a time
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Play/Pause sweeps a NOW cursor across two timelines; a button drops an obstacle; sliders change the blink interval and the sensor check period.
keyQuestions: Why can version A only see the obstacle when it wakes up?
What is the longest possible detection delay for version A with a 500 ms sleep?
How does version B keep the LED blinking on time without sleeping?
How many centimeters does the robot travel during each version's delay at 40 cm/s?
commonMisconceptions: The robot keeps reading its sensor while sleep() runs.
A shorter blink interval is the only way to make the robot react faster.
A non-blocking loop cannot blink the LED at a steady rate.
Plain subtraction of ticks_ms() values is always safe (ticks_diff() handles wrap-around).
assessmentOpportunities: Record detection delays for several obstacle times in a table and find version A's worst case.
Challenge: compute the distance traveled when the obstacle appears just after a 500 ms sleep starts (about 20 cm).
Exit ticket: rewrite a sleep-based blink loop to use ticks_ms() and ticks_diff().
